source.text: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ· Διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.

records.literal_gloss: And going out of him out of the temple says to him one of the disciples of him, Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going out of the temple, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!"
en.B: Jesus was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way out of the temple when one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples exclaimed to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, look! Such stones! Such buildings!"
en.R: Jesus was walking out of the temple courts. One of the disciples called out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, look at these huge stones! Look at these wonderful buildings!"

es.L: Y saliendo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} del templo, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice uno de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Maestro, ¡mira qué piedras y qué edificios!».
es.B: Jesús iba saliendo del templo cuando uno de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo admirado: «Maestro, ¡mira! ¡Qué piedras! ¡Qué edificios!».
es.R: Jesús iba saliendo de los patios del templo. Uno de los discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo en voz alta: «Maestro, ¡mira estas piedras tan enormes! ¡Mira estos edificios tan hermosos!».

sw.L: Naye alipokuwa akitoka hekaluni, mmoja wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anamwambia, "Mwalimu, tazama, mawe gani haya na majengo gani haya!"
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akitoka hekaluni, mmoja wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} alimwambia kwa mshangao, "Mwalimu, tazama! Mawe ya ajabu kama haya! Majengo ya ajabu kama haya!"
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akitoka katika viwanja vya hekalu. Mmoja wa wanafunzi alimwambia kwa sauti, "Mwalimu, tazama mawe haya makubwa sana! Tazama majengo haya mazuri!"

decisions.choice: says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, a past event is told in the present tense to make it vivid. The sense is past: he said.

decisions.choice: what stones, what buildings: an exclamation of wonder at their size and splendor
alternatives: a question about what kind of stones they were
decisions.reason: The word asks "of what sort", and here it marks amazement: what great stones, what fine buildings.

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts, rebuilt on a grand scale by Herod the Great
decisions.reason: Herod began rebuilding the temple about 20 BC, and work went on for decades. Some of its stones were enormous; blocks from the retaining walls can still be seen in Jerusalem. The word used here covers the whole complex, not only the sanctuary building.

decisions.choice: temple courts; huge stones; wonderful buildings
alternatives: the temple; what stones and what buildings
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus left the temple area and spells out what the disciple was admiring.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on separate pronouns and possessives only: él, le, sus
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb, where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English, as in Matthew 24 and Mark 16. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (le dice); past at Balanced and Readable (le dijo)
decisions.reason: Mark tells this in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: a span on the possessive wake; none on the subject and object prefixes (alipokuwa, anamwambia)
decisions.reason: Swahili carries "he" and "him" in prefixes inside the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Matthew. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (alimwambia)
decisions.reason: Mark tells this in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past.

source.text: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Βλέπεις ταύτας τὰς μεγάλας οἰκοδομάς;

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to him, See you these great buildings?

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings?
en.B: Jesus replied, "You see these great buildings?
en.R: Jesus answered, "Do you see these big buildings?

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «¿Ves estos grandes edificios?
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «¿Te fijas en estos grandes edificios?
es.R: Jesús le contestó: «¿Ves estos edificios tan grandes?

sw.L: Na Yesu akamwambia, "Unayaona majengo haya makubwa?
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Je, unayaona majengo haya makubwa?
sw.R: Yesu akamjibu, "Unaona majengo haya makubwa?

decisions.choice: Do you see these great buildings? a question that turns the disciple's wonder toward what will happen to them
alternatives: a statement: you see these great buildings
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a question or as a statement. Either way Jesus takes up the disciple's admiration and answers it with a warning.

decisions.choice: said to him: to the one disciple who spoke
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular. The answer is given to the disciple who spoke, though the others hear it.

decisions.choice: You see these great buildings?
alternatives: Do you see these great buildings?
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the question in the form of spoken English, with the voice rising at the end.

decisions.choice: le, ves: singular, to one disciple
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the one disciple who spoke (meaning decision m2), so Spanish uses the singular "tú" form; the plural forms and the ustedes / vosotros setting begin in 13:5, when he speaks to the four.

source.text: οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ μὴ καταλυθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: No not shall be left here stone upon stone which no not shall be thrown down.

en.L: There will not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down."
en.B: Not one stone here will be left resting on another. Every one will be pulled down."
en.R: Every one of them will be torn down. Not a single stone will be left on top of another."

es.L: De ningún modo quedará aquí piedra sobre piedra que no sea derribada».
es.B: No quedará aquí ni una piedra sobre otra. Todas serán derribadas».
es.R: Todos serán derribados. No quedará ni una sola piedra encima de otra».

sw.L: Hakika hapa halitaachwa jiwe juu ya jiwe ambalo halitabomolewa."
sw.B: Hakuna jiwe hata moja la hapa litakalobaki juu ya jingine. Yote yatabomolewa."
sw.R: Yote yatabomolewa. Hakuna hata jiwe moja litakalobaki juu ya jingine."

decisions.choice: will not, will not: two double negatives, a strong and certain prediction
decisions.reason: Each "no not" in the Greek is the strongest way of denying something. Jesus says the destruction will certainly be complete.

decisions.choice: be thrown down: a passive, the one who destroys is not named
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull down or demolish. The passive leaves the destroyer unnamed.

decisions.choice: the prediction of the temple's destruction
decisions.reason: Roman forces destroyed the temple in AD 70, when they took Jerusalem. Prophets had spoken in the same way about the first temple (Micah 3:12; Jeremiah 7:14; 26:18).

decisions.choice: Every one of them will be torn down. Not a single stone ...
alternatives: Not a stone will be left upon a stone that will not be thrown down
decisions.reason: Readable puts the main point first and then the picture of the stones, in two short sentences.

source.text: Καὶ καθημένου αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν Πέτρος καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀνδρέας·

records.literal_gloss: And sitting of him on the Mount of the Olives opposite the temple were asking him privately Peter and James and John and Andrew:

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately:
en.B: Then, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on the Mount of Olives facing the temple, four of them, Peter, James, John and Andrew, put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in private:
en.R: Later Jesus sat down on the Mount of Olives. From there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could see the temple across the valley. Peter, James, John, and Andrew came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a question:

es.L: Y estando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sentado en el monte de los Olivos, frente al templo, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban en privado Pedro y Santiago y Juan y Andrés:
es.B: Después, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba sentado en el monte de los Olivos, frente al templo, cuatro de ellos, Pedro, Santiago, Juan y Andrés, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hicieron una pregunta a solas:
es.R: Más tarde, Jesús se sentó en el monte de los Olivos. Desde allí podía ver el templo al otro lado del valle. Pedro, Santiago, Juan y Andrés se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron a solas y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hicieron una pregunta:

sw.L: Naye alipokuwa ameketi juu ya Mlima wa Mizeituni, mkabala na hekalu, Petro na Yakobo na Yohana na Andrea walikuwa wakimwuliza faraghani:
sw.B: Baadaye, alipokuwa ameketi juu ya Mlima wa Mizeituni, mkabala na hekalu, wanne kati yao, Petro, Yakobo, Yohana na Andrea, walimwuliza swali faraghani:
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu aliketi juu ya Mlima wa Mizeituni. Kutoka huko aliweza kuliona hekalu ng'ambo ya bonde. Petro, Yakobo, Yohana na Andrea walimwendea wakiwa peke yao, wakamwuliza swali:

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives opposite the temple: the ridge east of Jerusalem, looking down on the temple across the Kidron Valley
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives rises higher than the temple mount and faces it across a narrow valley. From there the whole temple could be seen.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: perhaps recalling the prophecy of the Lord standing there on the day of judgment
decisions.reason: Zechariah 14:4 says that on the day of the Lord his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives. Jesus' speech about the end is given on that same hill. Mark does not draw the link himself.

decisions.choice: privately: the four alone, apart from the others
decisions.reason: As in 4:34 and 9:28, the private setting marks teaching meant for the disciples. The four named are the first four called (1:16-20).

decisions.choice: From there he could see the temple across the valley; came to him
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "opposite" means here and says the four came to Jesus on their own.

source.text: Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα συντελεῖσθαι πάντα.

records.literal_gloss: Tell us, when these things will be, and what the sign when are about these things to be accomplished all?

en.L: "Tell us, when will these things be, and what [will be] the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?"
en.B: "Tell us, when will these things take place? And what sign will there be when all of them are about to reach their completion?"
en.R: "Tell us, when will this happen? What sign will show us that all these things are about to be completed?"

es.L: «Dinos, ¿cuándo será esto, y cuál [será] la señal de cuando todas estas cosas estén por cumplirse?».
es.B: «Dinos, ¿cuándo sucederá esto? ¿Y qué señal habrá cuando todo esto esté a punto de llegar a su cumplimiento?».
es.R: «Dinos, ¿cuándo pasará esto? ¿Qué señal nos mostrará que todas estas cosas están a punto de cumplirse?».

sw.L: "Tuambie, mambo haya yatakuwa lini, na [itakuwa] ishara gani wakati mambo haya yote yatakapokaribia kutimizwa?"
sw.B: "Tuambie, mambo haya yatatokea lini? Na kutakuwa na ishara gani mambo haya yote yatakapokaribia kukamilika?"
sw.R: "Tuambie, jambo hili litatokea lini? Ni ishara gani itakayotuonyesha kwamba mambo haya yote yanakaribia kutimia?"

decisions.choice: these things: the destruction of the temple Jesus has just foretold
alternatives: the end of the world in general
decisions.reason: The question picks up Jesus' words in 13:2. In the second half, "all these things" widens it to everything that goes with that event.

decisions.choice: be accomplished: be brought to completion, reach their end
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring to an end or to complete. It suggests that the disciples link the temple's fall with the close of the age.

decisions.choice: all these things ... be completed: perhaps echoing Daniel 12:7
decisions.reason: In Daniel 12:7 the angel says that when the power of the holy people is shattered, all these things will be completed. The disciples' words sound much the same.

decisions.choice: two questions: when, and what sign
decisions.reason: The disciples ask when, and how they will know it is near. The speech answers the second question at length and says in 13:32 that no one knows the day.

decisions.choice: reach their completion (B); be completed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for coming to an end.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἤρξατο λέγειν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus began to say to them, Take heed lest anyone you mislead.

en.L: And Jesus began to say to them, "Take care that no one misleads you.
en.B: Jesus began to speak to them: "Be on your guard, so that nobody leads you astray.
en.R: Jesus began to answer them. "Be careful! Do not let anyone fool you.

es.L: Y Jesús comenzó a decirles: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe.
es.B: Jesús comenzó a hablarles: «{{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} en guardia, para que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} extravíe.
es.R: Jesús comenzó a responderles. «¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe.

sw.L: Na Yesu alianza kuwaambia, "Angalieni mtu yeyote asiwapotoshe.
sw.B: Yesu alianza kusema nao, "Jihadharini, mtu asije akawapoteza.
sw.R: Yesu alianza kuwajibu. "Jihadharini! Msikubali mtu yeyote awadanganye.

decisions.choice: began to say: the start of a long speech that runs to the end of the chapter (13:37)
decisions.reason: This is the longest speech of Jesus in Mark. Everything to 13:37 is his answer to the four.

decisions.choice: take heed: look out, be on guard
decisions.reason: The verb is "see", used as a warning. It returns at 13:9, 13:23 and 13:33 and holds the speech together.

decisions.choice: mislead: lead astray, deceive
decisions.reason: The word means to make someone wander from the right way. The first danger Jesus names is deception, not suffering.

decisions.choice: take care (L); be on your guard (B); be careful (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the same English for this warning wherever it returns in the speech.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" and verb (miren|mirad, los|os)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the reader setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the speech, to 13:37.

decisions.choice: Miren (L), and the same verb in 13:9, 13:23 and 13:33
decisions.reason: The Greek says "look" each time Jesus warns them in this speech (meaning decision m2), so Literal keeps one word for it; Balanced and Readable say "estén en guardia" and "tengan cuidado", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Angalieni (L), and the same verb in 13:9, 13:23 and 13:33
decisions.reason: The Greek says "look" each time Jesus warns them in this speech (meaning decision m2), so Literal keeps one word for it; Balanced and Readable say "jihadharini" (be on guard), as the English says "be on your guard" and "be careful".

source.text: πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Many will come in the name of me saying that I am, and many they will mislead.

en.L: Many will come in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, 'I am [he],' and they will mislead many.
en.B: Many will come using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and saying, 'I am he,' and they will lead many astray.
en.R: Many people will come and use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. They will say, 'I am the one!' They will fool many people.

es.L: Muchos vendrán en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, diciendo: “Yo soy”, y engañarán a muchos.
es.B: Muchos vendrán usando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre y diciendo: “Yo soy él”, y extraviarán a muchos.
es.R: Mucha gente vendrá y usará {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Dirán: “¡Soy yo!”. Engañarán a mucha gente.

sw.L: Wengi watakuja katika jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, wakisema, 'Mimi ndiye,' nao watawapotosha wengi.
sw.B: Wengi watakuja wakilitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} na kusema, 'Mimi ndiye,' nao watawapoteza wengi.
sw.R: Watu wengi watakuja wakitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Watasema, 'Mimi ndiye yule!' Watawadanganya watu wengi.

decisions.choice: in my name: claiming my title or my authority
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to come claiming to act for them, or to be them. These people take for themselves what belongs to Jesus.

decisions.choice: I am: I am the one, the expected deliverer
alternatives: it is I, Jesus, come back
decisions.reason: The two words stand without anything after them. They mean "I am he": the one people are waiting for. Some read them as a claim to be Jesus himself returned.

decisions.choice: I am: the words Jesus himself uses at 6:50 and 14:62, which recall God's name in Exodus 3:14
decisions.reason: On Jesus' lips these words carry great weight. The deceivers will take them for themselves.

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); I am he (B); I am the one (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a word after "I am". Literal brackets it; Readable makes the claim plain.

decisions.choice: Yo soy (L); Yo soy él (B); ¡Soy yo! (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "Yo soy" can stand alone, so Literal supplies nothing and keeps the words that recall God's name (meaning decision m3). Balanced adds "él" and Readable says "¡Soy yo!" (it is me), the claim to be the one they expect (m2), without naming the Messiah, as the English does not.

decisions.choice: Mimi ndiye (L, B); Mimi ndiye yule (R), with nothing in brackets
decisions.reason: "Mimi ni" cannot end a sentence in Swahili. "Ndiye" already means "I am he, I am the one" (meaning decision m2), so Literal needs no bracket for the English "[he]"; Readable adds "yule" (that one), as the English says "the one".

source.text: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ γενέσθαι, ἀλλ’ οὔπω τὸ τέλος.

records.literal_gloss: When then you hear of wars and reports of wars, not be alarmed; it must happen, but not yet the end.

en.L: And when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed; it must happen, but the end [is] not yet.
en.B: When you hear of wars, and news of wars far away, do not be shaken. These things have to come, but that is not yet the end.
en.R: You will hear about wars close by and news of wars far away. Do not be afraid. These things must happen, but the end has not come yet.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:oigan|oigáis}} de guerras y rumores de guerras, no {{plural_you:se alarmen|os alarméis}}; es necesario que suceda, pero aún no [es] el fin.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:oigan|oigáis}} hablar de guerras, y de noticias de guerras lejanas, no {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}}. Estas cosas tienen que venir, pero eso no es todavía el fin.
es.R: {{plural_you:Oirán|Oiréis}} de guerras cercanas y noticias de guerras lejanas. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. Estas cosas tienen que pasar, pero todavía no ha llegado el fin.

sw.L: Na mtakaposikia vita na uvumi wa vita, msifadhaike; ni lazima yatokee, lakini mwisho bado.
sw.B: Mtakaposikia habari za vita, na habari za vita vya mbali, msitikiswe. Mambo hayo lazima yaje, lakini huo bado si mwisho.
sw.R: Mtasikia habari za vita vilivyo karibu na habari za vita vilivyo mbali. Msiogope. Mambo hayo lazima yatokee, lakini mwisho bado haujafika.

decisions.choice: reports of wars: news of wars elsewhere
decisions.reason: Wars nearby are heard; wars far off are heard about. The phrase covers both.

decisions.choice: it must happen: part of what God has planned
alternatives: it is bound to happen by chance
decisions.reason: "Must" here expresses God's purpose, as in Daniel 2:28: what must happen in the last days.

decisions.choice: the end: the end of the age
decisions.reason: War is not the signal that the end has come. The same word returns in 13:13.

decisions.choice: wars ... news of wars far away (B); wars close by and news of wars far away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the second phrase means instead of keeping the old pairing.

source.text: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, ἔσονται σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους, ἔσονται λιμοί· ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: Will rise up for nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom, there will be earthquakes in places, there will be famines; beginning of birth pains these.

en.L: For nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in [various] places; there will be famines. These [are the] beginning of birth pains.
en.B: Nation will go to war against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. Earthquakes will strike in one place after another, and there will be famines. All this is only the first of the birth pains.
en.R: Nations will fight against each other, and kingdoms will attack other kingdoms. There will be earthquakes in many places, and people will go hungry. But all this is only the start of the pain. It is like the first pains of a woman giving birth.

es.L: Porque se levantará nación contra nación y reino contra reino; habrá terremotos en [distintos] lugares; habrá hambrunas. Esto [es el] comienzo de [los] dolores de parto.
es.B: Una nación entrará en guerra contra otra, y un reino contra otro. Habrá terremotos en un lugar tras otro, y habrá hambrunas. Todo esto es solo el comienzo de los dolores de parto.
es.R: Unas naciones pelearán contra otras, y unos reinos atacarán a otros reinos. Habrá terremotos en muchos lugares, y la gente pasará hambre. Pero todo esto es solo el principio del dolor. Es como los primeros dolores de una mujer que va a dar a luz.

sw.L: Kwa maana taifa litainuka dhidi ya taifa na ufalme dhidi ya ufalme; kutakuwa na matetemeko ya ardhi mahali [mbalimbali]; kutakuwa na njaa. Haya [ni] mwanzo wa utungu wa kuzaa.
sw.B: Taifa litapigana na taifa, na ufalme na ufalme. Matetemeko ya ardhi yatatokea mahali pamoja baada ya pengine, na kutakuwa na njaa. Haya yote ni mwanzo tu wa utungu wa kuzaa.
sw.R: Mataifa yatapigana, na falme zitashambulia falme nyingine. Kutakuwa na matetemeko ya ardhi mahali pengi, na watu watakuwa na njaa. Lakini haya yote ni mwanzo tu wa maumivu. Ni kama uchungu wa kwanza wa mwanamke anayejifungua.

decisions.choice: nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom: in the words of Isaiah 19:2
decisions.reason: Isaiah 19:2 speaks of city against city and kingdom against kingdom, in God's judgment on Egypt. Jesus uses the prophets' language for the troubles ahead.

decisions.choice: the beginning of birth pains: the first of the sufferings that come before God's new age
alternatives: the start of the end itself
decisions.reason: The prophets used a woman's labor as a picture of the distress that comes before God acts (Isaiah 26:17-19; Micah 4:9-10). Birth pains are hard but lead to new life, and these are only the first of them.

decisions.choice: in places: here and there, in one place after another
decisions.reason: The phrase means throughout different places.

decisions.choice: there will be famines: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and troubles" after famines, a natural addition to the list. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: It is like the first pains of a woman giving birth
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of birth pains.

source.text: βλέπετε δὲ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτούς· παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς δαρήσεσθε καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων σταθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Take heed however you to yourselves; they will deliver up you to councils and in synagogues you will be beaten and before governors and kings you will stand because of me for a testimony to them.

en.L: But you, take care for yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and in synagogues you will be beaten, and before governors and kings you will stand because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as a testimony to them.
en.B: As for you, be on your guard. People will hand you over to the councils, and you will be flogged in the synagogues. You will stand before governors and kings for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, to bear witness to them.
en.R: Be careful about what will happen to you. People will take you to court. They will beat you in their meeting places. You will be put on trial in front of governors and kings because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. That way you will be able to tell them about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} por {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}}. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} entregarán a [los] consejos, y en [las] sinagogas {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} azotados, y ante gobernadores y reyes {{plural_you:comparecerán|compareceréis}} por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, como testimonio para ellos.
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:estén|estad}} en guardia. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} entregarán a los consejos, y {{plural_you:los|os}} azotarán en las sinagogas. {{plural_you:Comparecerán|Compareceréis}} ante gobernadores y reyes por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, para dar testimonio ante ellos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado con lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} va a pasar. La gente {{plural_you:los|os}} llevará a los tribunales. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} golpearán en sus lugares de reunión. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} juzgarán delante de gobernadores y reyes porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}}. Así {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} hablarles de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi jiangalieni wenyewe. Watawatoa ninyi kwa mabaraza, na katika masinagogi mtapigwa, na mbele ya magavana na wafalme mtasimamishwa kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kuwa ushahidi kwao.
sw.B: Kwa upande wenu, jihadharini. Watu watawapeleka kwenye mabaraza, nanyi mtachapwa viboko katika masinagogi. Mtasimama mbele ya magavana na wafalme kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ili mtoe ushahidi mbele yao.
sw.R: Jihadharini na yale yatakayowapata. Watu watawapeleka mahakamani. Watawapiga katika mahali pao pa kukusanyikia. Mtashtakiwa mbele ya watawala na wafalme kwa sababu mnanifuata. Kwa njia hiyo mtaweza kuwaeleza habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.

decisions.choice: they will hand over: the same verb used of John (1:14) and of Jesus himself (9:31; 10:33)
decisions.reason: The disciples will go the way their teacher goes: handed over to the authorities.

decisions.choice: councils, synagogues, beaten: local Jewish courts and the floggings they could order
decisions.reason: Local councils judged cases, and a synagogue could punish with a flogging of up to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:2-3). Paul received thirty-nine lashes five times (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: in synagogues you will be beaten: a new clause
alternatives: they will hand you over to councils and to synagogues; you will be beaten
decisions.reason: The phrase "in synagogues" could be joined to "hand over". The SBLGNT punctuation and the word order favor taking it with "you will be beaten".

decisions.choice: as a testimony to them: to bear witness about Jesus before them
decisions.reason: The same phrase in 6:11 means evidence against people. Here, before rulers and kings, it most likely means that the disciples' trials will give them a chance to speak about Jesus (compare 13:10).

decisions.choice: take you to court; meeting places; because you follow me; tell them about me
alternatives: councils; synagogues; because of me; as a testimony to them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the councils and synagogues and says what the testimony means. "Tell them about me" follows the reading chosen above.

decisions.choice: los consejos (L, B); los tribunales (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word names the local Jewish courts, not only the great council in Jerusalem (meaning decision m2). "Sanedrín" would point to that one council; "consejos" keeps the plural and the general sense, and Readable says what they did, as the English "take you to court".

decisions.choice: mabaraza (L, B), mahakamani (R); magavana (L, B), watawala (R)
decisions.reason: The councils are local Jewish courts (meaning decision m2), not only the Great Council in Jerusalem, so the plain plural "mabaraza"; Readable says "to court", as the English does. "Magavana" for the Roman governors, with the plainer "watawala" (rulers) at Readable, as across the New Testament drafts.

source.text: καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πρῶτον δεῖ κηρυχθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.

records.literal_gloss: And to all the nations first must be proclaimed the gospel.

en.L: And to all the nations the gospel must first be proclaimed.
en.B: And first the gospel has to be proclaimed to all the nations.
en.R: Before the end comes, the good news must be told to people of every nation.

es.L: Y a todas las naciones primero es necesario que sea proclamado el evangelio.
es.B: Y primero el evangelio tiene que ser proclamado a todas las naciones.
es.R: Antes de que llegue el fin, la buena noticia tiene que ser anunciada a la gente de todas las naciones.

sw.L: Na kwa mataifa yote kwanza ni lazima Injili ihubiriwe.
sw.B: Na kwanza ni lazima Injili ihubiriwe kwa mataifa yote.
sw.R: Kabla mwisho haujaja, habari njema lazima ielezwe kwa watu wa mataifa yote.

decisions.choice: first: before the end of 13:7
decisions.reason: "First" looks back to "not yet the end". The gospel will go to the nations before the end comes.

decisions.choice: must: God's plan, as in 13:7
decisions.reason: The same word as in 13:7. The spread of the gospel is part of what God has planned.

decisions.choice: to all the nations: begins a new sentence
alternatives: joined to 13:9: as a testimony to them and to all the nations
decisions.reason: Some read "to all the nations" with the end of 13:9. The SBLGNT begins a new sentence with it, and the word order supports that.

decisions.choice: Before the end comes
decisions.reason: Readable says what "first" is first to.

decisions.choice: el evangelio (L, B); la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "evangelio" names the message at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what the word means, as the English "good news" does.

decisions.choice: Injili (L, B); habari njema (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "Injili" names the message at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means, as the English "good news" does.

source.text: καὶ ὅταν ἄγωσιν ὑμᾶς παραδιδόντες, μὴ προμεριμνᾶτε τί λαλήσητε, ἀλλ’ ὃ ἐὰν δοθῇ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦτο λαλεῖτε, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑμεῖς οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον.

records.literal_gloss: And when they lead you, handing over, not be anxious beforehand what you should say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, this speak; not for are you those speaking but the Spirit the Holy.

en.L: And when they lead you [away], handing [you] over, do not be anxious beforehand about what you will say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
en.B: When they take you away to hand you over, do not be anxious in advance about what you will say. Whatever words are given to you in that hour, speak them. It will not be you who are speaking. It will be the Holy Spirit.
en.R: When you are arrested and put on trial, do not worry before it happens about what you will say. When the time comes, God will give you the words. Say what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives you. You will not be the one speaking. The Holy Spirit will speak through you.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} lleven, {{plural_you:entregándolos|entregándoos}}, no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} de antemano por lo que {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}, sino que lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} dé en aquella hora, eso {{plural_you:digan|decid}}; porque no {{plural_you:son ustedes los que hablan|sois vosotros los que habláis}}, sino el Espíritu Santo.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} lleven para {{plural_you:entregarlos|entregaros}}, no {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}} de antemano por lo que {{plural_you:van|vais}} a decir. {{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} las palabras que se {{plural_you:les|os}} den en aquella hora. No {{plural_you:serán ustedes los que hablen|seréis vosotros los que habléis}}; será el Espíritu Santo.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} arresten y {{plural_you:los|os}} lleven a juicio, no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} antes de tiempo por lo que {{plural_you:van|vais}} a decir. Cuando llegue el momento, Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dará las palabras. {{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dé. No {{plural_you:serán ustedes los que hablen|seréis vosotros los que habléis}}. El Espíritu Santo hablará por medio de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Na watakapowachukua, wakiwatoa, msihangaike kabla kuhusu mtakalosema, bali lolote mtakalopewa saa ile, hilo ndilo mseme; kwa maana si ninyi mnaosema, bali Roho Mtakatifu.
sw.B: Watakapowachukua ili kuwakabidhi, msiwe na wasiwasi mapema juu ya mtakalosema. Maneno yoyote mtakayopewa saa ile, yasemeni hayo. Si ninyi mtakaokuwa mkisema; ni Roho Mtakatifu.
sw.R: Mtakapokamatwa na kushtakiwa, msihangaike kabla ya wakati huo kuhusu mtakalosema. Wakati utakapofika, Mungu atawapa maneno. Semeni yale atakayowapa. Si ninyi mtakaosema. Roho Mtakatifu atasema kupitia ninyi.

decisions.choice: is given: a passive, God is the giver
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. The end of the verse names the Holy Spirit as the one who speaks.

decisions.choice: in that hour: at that moment, when you are on trial
decisions.reason: "Hour" here means the time when something happens.

decisions.choice: the Spirit speaking for them: like God's promise to Moses
decisions.reason: When Moses feared to speak before Pharaoh, God promised to be with his mouth and teach him what to say (Exodus 4:12).

decisions.choice: arrested and put on trial; God will give you the words
alternatives: they lead you away, handing you over; is given
decisions.reason: Readable says what being led away and handed over means and names God as the giver.

decisions.choice: one plural_you span over the whole phrase: {{plural_you:son ustedes los que hablan|sois vosotros los que habláis}}
alternatives: separate spans on son, ustedes and hablan
decisions.reason: In Spanish the verb after "los que" agrees with "ustedes" or "vosotros", so all three words change together; a single span keeps each form whole.

source.text: καὶ παραδώσει ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: And will deliver up brother brother to death and father child, and will rise up children against parents and will put to death them.

en.L: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father [his] child, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.
en.B: Brothers will hand their brothers over to be killed, and fathers their children. Children will rise up against their parents and send them to their deaths.
en.R: Families will turn against each other. Brothers will hand their own brothers over to be killed. Fathers will do this to their children. Children will turn against their parents and have them killed.

es.L: Y el hermano entregará a muerte al hermano, y el padre al hijo, y se levantarán hijos contra padres y los harán morir.
es.B: Los hermanos entregarán a sus hermanos para que los maten, y los padres a sus hijos. Los hijos se rebelarán contra sus padres y los enviarán a la muerte.
es.R: Las familias se pondrán unas contra otras. Los hermanos entregarán a sus propios hermanos para que los maten. Los padres harán lo mismo con sus hijos. Los hijos se volverán contra sus padres y harán que los maten.

sw.L: Na ndugu atamtoa ndugu kwa kifo, na baba [atamtoa] mtoto, na watoto watainuka dhidi ya wazazi na kuwafanya wauawe.
sw.B: Ndugu atamkabidhi ndugu yake auawe, na baba atamkabidhi mtoto wake. Watoto wataasi wazazi wao na kuwapeleka wauawe.
sw.R: Watu wa familia moja watageukana. Ndugu watawakabidhi ndugu zao wenyewe ili wauawe. Akina baba watawafanyia watoto wao vivyo hivyo. Watoto watawageuka wazazi wao na kuwafanya wauawe.

decisions.choice: children against parents: in the words of Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Micah 7:6 describes a time when a son treats his father with contempt and a daughter rises against her mother, and a person's enemies are in their own household.

decisions.choice: put them to death: cause them to be executed, by handing them over to the authorities
alternatives: kill them with their own hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring about someone's death. In context it means betraying them to the courts.

decisions.choice: will hand over: the same verb as in 13:9 and 13:11
decisions.reason: The handing over now comes from inside the family.

decisions.choice: Families will turn against each other.
decisions.reason: Readable begins with a short sentence that says what the verse describes.

source.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.

records.literal_gloss: And you will be hated by all because of the name of me.

en.L: And you will be hated by all because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.B: Everyone will hate you because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.R: Everyone will hate you because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} odiados por todos a causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.
es.B: Todos {{plural_you:los|os}} odiarán por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.
es.R: Todo el mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} odiará porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}}.

sw.L: Nanyi mtachukiwa na wote kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.
sw.B: Kila mtu atawachukia kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.
sw.R: Kila mtu atawachukia kwa sababu ninyi ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you bear my name and belong to me
alternatives: because you speak my name aloud
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. They will be hated for being known as Jesus' followers.

decisions.choice: by all: by people everywhere
decisions.reason: "All" is a strong general word: they will meet hatred on every side.

decisions.choice: because you belong to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my name" means here.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: The however having endured to end this will be saved.

en.L: But the one who has endured to [the] end, this one will be saved.
en.B: But whoever holds out to the end will be saved.
en.R: But those who do not give up, right to the end, will be saved.

es.L: Pero el que haya perseverado hasta [el] fin, ese será salvo.
es.B: Pero quien se mantenga firme hasta el fin será salvo.
es.R: Pero los que no se den por vencidos, hasta el final, serán salvados.

sw.L: Lakini yeye aliyevumilia hadi mwisho, huyo ataokolewa.
sw.B: Lakini yeyote atakayesimama imara mpaka mwisho ataokolewa.
sw.R: Lakini wale wasiokata tamaa, mpaka mwisho kabisa, wataokolewa.

decisions.choice: endured: held out, stayed faithful under pressure
decisions.reason: The verb means to remain under a burden without giving way. Here it means staying loyal to Jesus while hated and handed over.

decisions.choice: to the end: to the very end, whether of one's life or of the time of trouble
alternatives: to the end of the age only
decisions.reason: There is no article, and the phrase can mean completely, to the last. It may also look back to "the end" in 13:7.

decisions.choice: will be saved: final salvation by God, not escape from death
decisions.reason: Some of these believers will be put to death (13:12). The promise is that God will save them in the end.

decisions.choice: whoever holds out (B); those who do not give up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for enduring. The Greek speaks of anyone, so no male form is needed.

source.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω μηδὲ εἰσελθάτω τι ἆραι ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: When then you see the abomination of the desolation standing where not it must, the one reading let him understand, then those in Judea let them flee to the mountains, \v 15 the one upon the housetop not let him come down nor go in anything to take out of the house of him, \v 16 and the one in the field not let him return to the things behind to take the cloak of him.

en.L: But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where he must not (let the one reading understand), then let those in Judea flee to the mountains; \v 15 let the one on the housetop not come down nor go in to take anything out of {{gender:their|his}} house, \v 16 and let the one in the field not turn back to the things behind to take {{gender:their|his}} cloak.
en.B: But when you see the abomination that brings ruin standing where he has no right to be (let the reader take note), then those who are in Judea must escape to the hills. \v 15 Anyone who is on the roof must not go down into the house to fetch anything out of it. \v 16 Anyone who is out in the field must not go back for a cloak.
en.R: One day you will see 'the horrible thing that destroys' standing where he should not stand. (Reader, think carefully about what this means.) When that happens, people in Judea must run away to the hills. \v 15 If someone is up on the roof of a house, they must not go down and go inside to get anything. \v 16 If someone is working in the field, they must not go back to get their coat.

es.L: Pero cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} la abominación de la desolación en pie donde él no debe [estar] (quien lea, que entienda), entonces los que estén en Judea huyan a las montañas; \v 15 el que esté sobre la azotea no baje ni entre a llevarse nada de su casa, \v 16 y el que esté en el campo no se vuelva a lo que dejó atrás para llevarse su manto.
es.B: Pero cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} la abominación que trae la ruina, de pie donde él no tiene derecho a estar (que el lector preste atención), entonces los que estén en Judea deben escapar a las montañas. \v 15 El que esté en la azotea no debe bajar ni entrar en la casa a buscar nada. \v 16 El que esté en el campo no debe volver a buscar su manto.
es.R: Un día {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} “la cosa horrible que destruye” de pie donde él no debe estar. (Lector, piensa bien lo que esto significa). Cuando eso pase, la gente que esté en Judea tiene que huir a las montañas. \v 15 Si alguien está arriba, en el techo de una casa, no debe bajar ni entrar a sacar nada. \v 16 Si alguien está trabajando en el campo, no debe volver a buscar su abrigo.

sw.L: Lakini mtakapoona kitu cha machukizo kiletacho ukiwa amesimama mahali asipopaswa (msomaji na aelewe), hapo walioko Yudea na wakimbie milimani; \v 15 aliye juu ya paa asishuke wala asiingie kuchukua kitu chochote nyumbani mwake, \v 16 na aliye shambani asirudi nyuma kuchukua joho lake.
sw.B: Lakini mtakapoona machukizo yaletayo maangamizi amesimama mahali asipostahili kuwa (msomaji na azingatie), wale walioko Yudea lazima wakimbilie milimani. \v 15 Aliye juu ya paa asishuke kuingia nyumbani ili kuchukua kitu chochote. \v 16 Aliye shambani asirudi kuchukua joho lake.
sw.R: Siku moja mtaona 'kitu kibaya cha kuchukiza kinachoangamiza' amesimama mahali asipopaswa kusimama. (Msomaji, fikiri kwa makini maana yake.) Hilo likitokea, watu walioko Yudea lazima wakimbilie milimani. \v 15 Mtu akiwa juu ya paa la nyumba, asishuke na kuingia ndani kuchukua kitu chochote. \v 16 Mtu akiwa anafanya kazi shambani, asirudi kuchukua koti lake.

decisions.choice: the abomination of desolation: the phrase from Daniel 9:27, 11:31 and 12:11
decisions.reason: In Daniel it is a detestable thing set up in God's sanctuary that leaves it desolate. In 167 BC the Syrian king Antiochus IV set up a pagan altar on the temple altar, and 1 Maccabees 1:54 uses the same phrase for it. Jesus says something like it will happen again.

decisions.choice: standing: a masculine participle, pointing to a person
alternatives: it standing: a thing, matching the noun
decisions.reason: The noun "abomination" is neuter, but "standing" is masculine. That suggests a person: someone who stands where only God belongs. Mark does not say who.

decisions.choice: where he must not: in the holy place, the temple
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of the sanctuary, and Matthew 24:15 says "in the holy place". Mark keeps the phrase veiled.

decisions.choice: let the one reading understand: an aside to the reader
alternatives: Jesus telling his hearers to read Daniel carefully
decisions.reason: The words speak of reading, not hearing, so they are most likely Mark's own words to those who read his book aloud or to themselves. They urge the reader to see what the veiled phrase means.

decisions.choice: the housetop, the cloak: flat roofs used as living space, and the outer garment laid aside for work
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs reached by an outside stair, so one could leave without going in. A worker in the field would lay the outer cloak aside. The danger will be so sudden that there is no time even for these.

decisions.choice: their or his (L); anyone ... a cloak (B); someone ... they (R)
alternatives: let him ... his house ... his cloak
decisions.reason: The commands are general and apply to anyone. Literal offers "their" or "his" through the gender setting; Balanced and Readable use "anyone" and "they".

decisions.choice: the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that destroys (R); let the reader take note (B); Reader, think carefully about what this means (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Daniel's phrase as it is. Balanced and Readable say what it means. All levels keep Mark's aside in parentheses.

decisions.choice: la abominación de la desolación (L); la abominación que trae la ruina (B); la cosa horrible que destruye (R); de pie donde él no debe estar
decisions.reason: Daniel's phrase (meaning decision m1): Literal keeps its form, Balanced and Readable say what the desolation is, as the English does. The Greek "standing" is masculine and may point to a person (m2, uncertain); a Spanish participle would have to agree with the feminine "abominación", so "de pie" with "él" keeps that hint, as the English "he" does.

decisions.choice: su casa, su manto, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal has "their" or "his" under the gender setting. Spanish "su" already serves for both, so there is nothing for the setting to change, as in Matthew 24:17-18. The same with "su trabajo" in 13:34.

decisions.choice: amesimama mahali asipopaswa: the person prefix a- after a thing noun
decisions.reason: The Greek "standing" is masculine although "abomination" is neuter, which may point to a person (meaning decision m2, uncertain). Swahili can show the same shift: the verb takes the person prefix a- ("amesimama") instead of agreeing with "kitu" or "machukizo", as the English says "he". Daniel's phrase (m1) is worded as in Matthew 24:15.

decisions.choice: nyumbani mwake, joho lake, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal has "their" or "his" under the gender setting. Swahili "-ake" already means either, so there is nothing for the setting to change. The same with "kazi yake" in 13:34.

source.text: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

records.literal_gloss: Woe then to those in womb having and to those nursing in those days.

en.L: And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
en.B: How terrible it will be in those days for women who are expecting a child or nursing a baby!
en.R: Those days will be very hard for women who are going to have a baby, and for mothers who are feeding babies.

es.L: ¡Y ay de las que tengan [un hijo] en el vientre y de las que amamanten en aquellos días!
es.B: ¡Ay de las mujeres que en aquellos días estén esperando un hijo o amamantando a un bebé!
es.R: Aquellos días serán muy difíciles para las mujeres que van a tener un bebé y para las madres que están dando el pecho a sus bebés.

sw.L: Lakini ole wao wenye [watoto] tumboni na wale wanaonyonyesha katika siku hizo!
sw.B: Ole wao wanawake wenye mimba na wale wanaonyonyesha watoto katika siku hizo!
sw.R: Siku hizo zitakuwa ngumu sana kwa wanawake wajawazito, na kwa akina mama wanaonyonyesha watoto wachanga.

decisions.choice: having in the womb: pregnant
decisions.reason: "To have in the womb" is the ordinary Greek way of saying a woman is pregnant.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and pity
decisions.reason: Here "woe" is not a curse on these women. It grieves for them, because they will find it hardest to flee.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be (B); will be very hard (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the cry of pity in current English.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay de...! (L, B)
alternatives: ¡Qué terrible será...! (B), as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: The cry of grief and pity (meaning decision m2) is "¡ay!" at Literal and Balanced across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 24:19; Spanish still uses it in this sense. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Ole wao (L, B)
alternatives: Itakuwa vibaya sana (B), as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: The cry of grief and pity (meaning decision m2) is "ole" at Literal and Balanced across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 24:19. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται χειμῶνος·

records.literal_gloss: Pray then that not it happen in winter.

en.L: And pray that it may not happen in winter.
en.B: Pray that this does not come in winter.
en.R: Pray that it will not happen in the winter.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} para que no suceda en invierno.
es.B: {{plural_you:Oren|Orad}} para que esto no llegue en invierno.
es.R: {{plural_you:Oren|Orad}} para que no suceda en el invierno.

sw.L: Na salini ili lisitokee wakati wa masika.
sw.B: Ombeni jambo hili lisije likatokea wakati wa masika.
sw.R: Ombeni kwamba lisitokee wakati wa masika ya baridi.

decisions.choice: winter: the cold, rainy season
decisions.reason: In Judea winter is the rainy season. Streams in the valleys run high and roads turn to mud, so flight on foot would be hard.

decisions.choice: it: the time of flight and trouble just described
decisions.reason: There is no stated subject. The sense is that the time of flight should not fall in winter.

decisions.choice: that it not happen in winter: the SBLGNT reading
alternatives: that your flight not happen in winter
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "your flight", as in Matthew 24:20, making the subject clear. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: wakati wa masika (L, B); wakati wa masika ya baridi (R)
decisions.reason: Winter in Judea is the cold, rainy season (meaning decision m1), when roads are mud and streams flood. "Masika", the long rains, names that kind of season better than "baridi" (cold) alone; Readable adds the cold, as in Matthew 24:20.

source.text: ἔσονται γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι θλῖψις οἵα οὐ γέγονεν τοιαύτη ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἣν ἔκτισεν ὁ θεὸς ἕως τοῦ νῦν καὶ οὐ μὴ γένηται.

records.literal_gloss: Will be for the days those tribulation such as not has happened such from beginning of creation which created God until the now and no not will happen.

en.L: For those days will be tribulation such as has not happened from [the] beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will.
en.B: For those days will bring distress unlike any there has been from the beginning, when God created the world, until now, or ever will be again.
en.R: That will be a time of terrible trouble. Nothing like it has happened since God made the world, and nothing like it will ever happen again.

es.L: Porque aquellos días serán tribulación, cual no ha habido semejante desde [el] principio de la creación que creó Dios hasta ahora, y no la habrá jamás.
es.B: Porque aquellos días traerán una angustia como no la ha habido desde el principio, cuando Dios creó el mundo, hasta ahora, ni la habrá nunca más.
es.R: Será un tiempo de problemas terribles. Nunca ha pasado nada parecido desde que Dios hizo el mundo, y nunca volverá a pasar nada igual.

sw.L: Kwa maana siku hizo zitakuwa dhiki, ya namna isiyowahi kutokea tangu mwanzo wa uumbaji ambao Mungu aliumba hadi sasa, wala haitatokea kamwe.
sw.B: Kwa maana siku hizo zitaleta taabu ambayo haijawahi kuwako tangu mwanzo, Mungu alipoumba ulimwengu, mpaka sasa, wala haitakuwako tena kamwe.
sw.R: Utakuwa wakati wa taabu mbaya sana. Hakuna kitu kama hicho kilichowahi kutokea tangu Mungu alipoumba ulimwengu, na hakitatokea tena kamwe.

decisions.choice: tribulation such as has not happened: in the words of Daniel 12:1
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:1 speaks of a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation until that time. Jesus widens it to the whole of creation.

decisions.choice: those days will be tribulation: those days will be a time of great distress
decisions.reason: The days are described as being the distress itself, a strong way of saying what will fill them.

decisions.choice: the creation which God created: a doubled phrase that stresses the whole span of time
decisions.reason: Saying the same thing twice is a Hebrew way of adding weight: since the very beginning of everything God made.

decisions.choice: never will: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strong denial again: there will never be another time like it.

decisions.choice: tribulation (L); distress (B); terrible trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the long-used word. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for great suffering and pressure.

source.text: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολόβωσεν κύριος τὰς ἡμέρας, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ.

records.literal_gloss: And if not had shortened Lord the days, not would have been saved any flesh.

en.L: And if [the] Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved.
en.B: If the Lord had not cut those days short, no one at all would survive.
en.R: If the Lord had not made that time shorter, no one would live through it.

es.L: Y si [el] Señor no hubiera acortado los días, no se habría salvado ninguna carne.
es.B: Si el Señor no hubiera acortado aquellos días, nadie en absoluto sobreviviría.
es.R: Si el Señor no hubiera hecho más corto ese tiempo, nadie quedaría con vida.

sw.L: Na kama Bwana asingalizifupisha siku, hakuna mwili wowote ungaliokolewa.
sw.B: Kama Bwana asingalizifupisha siku hizo, hakuna mtu hata mmoja ambaye angesalimika.
sw.R: Kama Bwana asingaliufupisha wakati huo, hakuna mtu ambaye angeishi hadi mwisho wake.

decisions.choice: Lord: God
decisions.reason: Here "Lord" means God, as the next sentence shows: the one who chose the elect.

decisions.choice: any flesh: any human being
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for living people. "No flesh" means no one.

decisions.choice: be saved: survive, come through alive
decisions.reason: Here the word speaks of living through the distress, not of salvation at the end as in 13:13.

decisions.choice: had shortened: the past tense speaks of a decision God has already made
decisions.reason: The days have not yet come, but God has already decided to cut them short.

decisions.choice: survive (B); live through it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that physical survival is meant.

source.text: ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἐκολόβωσεν τὰς ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: But because of the elect whom he chose he shortened the days.

en.L: But because of the elect, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shortened the days.
en.B: But because of the chosen, those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cut the days short.
en.R: But God has chosen people to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. For their sake {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made that time shorter.

es.L: Pero por causa de los elegidos, a quienes escogió, acortó los días.
es.B: Pero por causa de los elegidos, los que escogió para {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}}, ha acortado esos días.
es.R: Pero Dios ha elegido a un pueblo para que sea {{deity_pronoun:suyo|Suyo}}. Por amor a ellos ha hecho más corto ese tiempo.

sw.L: Lakini kwa ajili ya wateule aliowachagua, alizifupisha siku.
sw.B: Lakini kwa ajili ya waliochaguliwa, wale aliowachagua kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, amezifupisha siku hizo.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu amewachagua watu wawe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Kwa ajili yao ameufupisha wakati huo.

decisions.choice: the elect: the people God has chosen, his people
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the chosen are God's people. Here they are those who belong to God through Jesus (13:22, 27).

decisions.choice: chose: a middle form, chose for himself
decisions.reason: The form stresses that God chose them to be his own.

decisions.choice: the elect whom he chose: a doubled phrase that stresses God's choice
decisions.reason: As in 13:19, the repeated root adds weight.

decisions.choice: God has chosen people to be his own
alternatives: because of the elect whom he chose
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what "the elect" means.

decisions.choice: wateule (L); waliochaguliwa (B); watu ... amewachagua (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "wateule" (the elect) at Literal, and the plainer "waliochaguliwa" (those who have been chosen) at Balanced, which also keeps the link with "aliowachagua" (meaning decision m3).

source.text: καὶ τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἴδε ὧδε ὁ χριστός, Ἴδε ἐκεῖ, μὴ πιστεύετε·

records.literal_gloss: And then if anyone to you says, Look, here the Christ, look, there, not believe.

en.L: And then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here [is] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},' 'Look, there,' do not believe [it].
en.B: At that time, if anyone tells you, 'See, here is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}!' or 'See, there he is!' do not believe it.
en.R: At that time someone may say to you, 'Look, here is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}!' or 'Look, he is over there!' Do not believe it.

es.L: Y entonces, si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} dice: “{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, aquí [está] el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}”, “{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, allí”, no [lo] {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}.
es.B: En ese tiempo, si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} dice: “{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, aquí está el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}”, o “{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, allí está”, no lo {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}.
es.R: En ese tiempo alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} podrá decir: “¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, aquí está el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}!”, o “¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, está allá!”. No lo {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}.

sw.L: Na wakati huo mtu yeyote akiwaambia, 'Tazameni, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} [yuko] hapa,' 'Tazameni, [yuko] kule,' msiamini.
sw.B: Wakati huo, mtu yeyote akiwaambia, 'Tazameni, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} yuko hapa!' au 'Tazameni, yuko kule!' msiamini.
sw.R: Wakati huo mtu anaweza kuwaambia, 'Tazameni, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} yuko hapa!' au 'Tazameni, yuko kule!' Msiamini.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: "Christ" is the Greek for the Hebrew title Messiah, the Anointed One. People will claim the promised king has appeared.

decisions.choice: then: in that time of distress
decisions.reason: "Then" ties the warning to the days just described.

decisions.choice: do not believe: a present command, do not go on believing such claims
alternatives: do not listen to them at all
decisions.reason: The command is plain: refuse to believe such reports, however often they come.

decisions.choice: 'Look, there' (L); 'See, there he is!' (B); 'Look, he is over there!' (R)
decisions.reason: Greek gives only "look, there". Balanced and Readable add "or" and "he is" to make the second claim a full saying.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, with the article outside the span
alternatives: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article: "the Christ", the Messiah as a title (meaning decision m1). Spanish keeps "el" with both wordings, so only the noun changes, as in Matthew 24:23.

source.text: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πρὸς τὸ ἀποπλανᾶν εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·

records.literal_gloss: Will arise for false-christs and false-prophets and will give signs and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, the elect.

en.L: For false {{christos:christs|messiahs}} and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, the elect.
en.B: For false {{christos:christs|messiahs}} and false prophets will rise up and do signs and wonders, so as to lead the chosen ones astray, if that could be done.
en.R: People will come who falsely claim to be {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Others will falsely claim to be prophets. They will do signs and amazing things to fool God's chosen people, if they can.

es.L: Porque se levantarán falsos {{christos:cristos|mesías}} y falsos profetas, y darán señales y prodigios para engañar, si [fuera] posible, a los elegidos.
es.B: Porque surgirán falsos {{christos:cristos|mesías}} y falsos profetas, y harán señales y prodigios para extraviar a los elegidos, si eso pudiera hacerse.
es.R: Vendrán personas que dirán falsamente que son el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}. Otros dirán falsamente que son profetas. Harán señales y cosas asombrosas para engañar al pueblo que Dios ha elegido, si pueden.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{christos:makristo|masihi}} wa uongo na manabii wa uongo watainuka, nao watatoa ishara na maajabu ili kuwapotosha, kama ikiwezekana, wateule.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{christos:makristo|masihi}} wa uongo na manabii wa uongo watatokea, nao watafanya ishara na maajabu ili kuwapoteza waliochaguliwa, kama jambo hilo lingewezekana.
sw.R: Watakuja watu wanaodai kwa uongo kwamba wao ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Wengine watadai kwa uongo kwamba ni manabii. Watafanya ishara na mambo ya kushangaza ili kuwadanganya watu wa Mungu aliowachagua, kama wakiweza.

decisions.choice: false christs: people who falsely claim to be the Messiah
decisions.reason: The word joins "false" and "Christ". It means pretenders to the title of Messiah.

decisions.choice: false prophets with signs and wonders: as in Deuteronomy 13:1-3
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 13:1-3 warns that a prophet may give a sign or wonder that comes true and still lead people after other gods. Signs alone do not prove a messenger is from God.

decisions.choice: if possible: they will try, though it may not be possible
decisions.reason: The phrase shows how strong the deception will be. It also hints that God will keep his chosen ones from being led away.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: works that seem to show power from God
decisions.reason: The pair is the Old Testament phrase for God's mighty acts, as in Egypt (Deuteronomy 6:22).

decisions.choice: who falsely claim to be the Messiah; God's chosen people
alternatives: false Christs, false prophets; the elect
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two compound words mean and whose chosen people they are.

decisions.choice: {{christos:makristo|masihi}} wa uongo
decisions.reason: The Greek is a plural, false christs (meaning decision m1). Swahili makes the plural of "Kristo" with ma-, while "masihi" is the same in the plural, so the span covers the whole word, as in Matthew 24:24.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ βλέπετε· προείρηκα ὑμῖν πάντα.

records.literal_gloss: You however take heed; I have foretold to you all things.

en.L: But you, take care; I have told you all things beforehand.
en.B: So you must be on your guard. I have told you all of it in advance.
en.R: So be careful! I have warned you about all this before it happens.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}; {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} he dicho todo de antemano.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:estén|estad}} en guardia. {{plural_you:Se lo|Os lo}} he dicho todo de antemano.
es.R: ¡Así que {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} cuidado! {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he advertido de todo esto antes de que suceda.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi angalieni; nimewaambia mambo yote mapema.
sw.B: Basi ninyi jihadharini. Nimewaambia yote mapema.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo jihadharini! Nimewaonya juu ya mambo haya yote kabla hayajatokea.

decisions.choice: you: stressed, you as opposed to those who are misled
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis: whatever others do, you be on guard.

decisions.choice: all things: everything they need to know about these events
decisions.reason: Jesus has told them all they need to keep from being deceived, not every detail of what will happen.

decisions.choice: warned you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the telling is for.

source.text: Ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν ἐκείνην ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες ἔσονται ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πίπτοντες, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς σαλευθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: But in those days after the tribulation that the sun will be darkened, and the moon not will give the light of it, \v 25 and the stars will be out of the heaven falling, and the powers that in the heavens will be shaken.

en.L: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, \v 25 and the stars will be falling out of heaven, and the powers that [are] in the heavens will be shaken.
en.B: But in those days, after that time of distress, the sun will grow dark and the moon will give no light. \v 25 Stars will come falling from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
en.R: In those days, after that time of terrible trouble, the sun will become dark. The moon will not shine. \v 25 Stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the heavens will be shaken.

es.L: Pero en aquellos días, después de aquella tribulación, el sol se oscurecerá, y la luna no dará su resplandor, \v 25 y las estrellas estarán cayendo del cielo, y los poderes que [están] en los cielos serán sacudidos.
es.B: Pero en aquellos días, después de aquel tiempo de angustia, el sol se oscurecerá y la luna no dará su luz. \v 25 Las estrellas caerán del cielo, y los poderes de los cielos serán sacudidos.
es.R: En aquellos días, después de ese tiempo de problemas terribles, el sol se pondrá oscuro. La luna no brillará. \v 25 Las estrellas caerán del cielo. Los poderes que hay en los cielos serán sacudidos.

sw.L: Lakini katika siku hizo, baada ya dhiki ile, jua litatiwa giza, na mwezi hautatoa mwanga wake, \v 25 na nyota zitakuwa zikianguka kutoka mbinguni, na nguvu zilizo mbinguni zitatikiswa.
sw.B: Lakini katika siku hizo, baada ya wakati ule wa taabu, jua litakuwa giza na mwezi hautatoa mwanga wake. \v 25 Nyota zitaanguka kutoka angani, na nguvu za mbinguni zitatikiswa.
sw.R: Katika siku hizo, baada ya wakati ule wa taabu mbaya, jua litakuwa giza. Mwezi hautang'aa. \v 25 Nyota zitaanguka kutoka angani. Nguvu zilizoko mbinguni zitatikiswa.

decisions.choice: sun, moon and stars: in the words of Isaiah 13:10 and 34:4
alternatives: a new prophecy with no source
decisions.reason: Isaiah 13:10 says the sun will be dark and the moon will not give its light; Isaiah 34:4 says the host of heaven will fall. Joel 2:10 and 3:15 speak the same way.

decisions.choice: darkened sun and falling stars: the prophets' language for God acting in judgment
alternatives: only a description of the physical sky
decisions.reason: Isaiah used these words about the fall of Babylon (Isaiah 13). Such language marks a great act of God that shakes the world. How literally it is meant here is not certain.

decisions.choice: the powers in the heavens: the heavenly bodies, or spiritual powers ruling there
decisions.reason: "Powers" can mean the sun, moon and stars as the host of heaven, or spiritual beings. Both were thought of together.

decisions.choice: in those days, after that tribulation: a new stage after the distress of 13:14-23
alternatives: the same moment as the distress
decisions.reason: "But" and "after" mark a turn from the troubles to what follows them.

decisions.choice: sky
decisions.reason: The same Greek word means both sky and heaven. Where stars fall, Balanced and Readable say sky.

source.text: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλαις μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς καὶ δόξης·

records.literal_gloss: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with power great and glory.

en.L: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
en.B: Then people will see the Son of Man come in clouds, with great power and glory.
en.R: Then everyone will see the Son of Man come in the clouds. He will come with great power and glory.

es.L: Y entonces verán al Hijo del Hombre que viene en nubes con gran poder y gloria.
es.B: Entonces la gente verá al Hijo del Hombre venir en las nubes, con gran poder y gloria.
es.R: Entonces todo el mundo verá al Hijo del Hombre venir en las nubes. Vendrá con gran poder y gloria.

sw.L: Na hapo watamwona Mwana wa Adamu akija katika mawingu pamoja na nguvu nyingi na utukufu.
sw.B: Ndipo watu watakapomwona Mwana wa Adamu akija katika mawingu, akiwa na nguvu kubwa na utukufu.
sw.R: Kisha kila mtu atamwona Mwana wa Adamu akija katika mawingu. Atakuja akiwa na nguvu kubwa na utukufu.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in clouds: Daniel 7:13
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is given authority and a kingdom that will never end. Jesus uses the title of himself throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: coming: the Son of Man coming in glory at the end
alternatives: only his going up to God to be crowned
decisions.reason: In Daniel the son of man comes to the Ancient of Days. Some read Jesus' words as his going to God in triumph. The angels gathering the elect in 13:27 point to his coming to earth.

decisions.choice: they will see: people in general
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It means people will see.

decisions.choice: people (B); everyone (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The title used across the New Testament drafts. "Hombre" here means humankind, as in Daniel 7:13 (meaning decision m1), and the title is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The title used across the New Testament drafts, as in John: "Adamu" also means humankind (meaning decision m1, Daniel 7:13). "Mwana wa Mtu" is closer to the Greek words; a reviewer should weigh it.

source.text: καὶ τότε ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἐπισυνάξει τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπ’ ἄκρου γῆς ἕως ἄκρου οὐρανοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And then he will send the angels and will gather together the elect from the four winds from end of earth to end of heaven.

en.L: And then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out the angels and will gather together the elect from the four winds, from [the] end of earth to [the] end of heaven.
en.B: And then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out the angels and gather the chosen ones from all four winds, from the farthest edge of the earth to the farthest edge of the sky.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out the angels. They will gather God's chosen people from every direction, from one end of the earth and sky to the other.

es.L: Y entonces enviará a los ángeles y reunirá a los elegidos de los cuatro vientos, desde [el] extremo de [la] tierra hasta [el] extremo del cielo.
es.B: Y entonces enviará a los ángeles y reunirá a los elegidos de los cuatro vientos, desde el último confín de la tierra hasta el último confín del cielo.
es.R: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} enviará a los ángeles. Ellos reunirán al pueblo que Dios ha elegido, de todas partes, de un extremo a otro de la tierra y del cielo.

sw.L: Na hapo atawatuma malaika, na kuwakusanya wateule kutoka upepo wa pande nne, kutoka mwisho wa nchi hadi mwisho wa mbingu.
sw.B: Kisha atawatuma malaika na kuwakusanya waliochaguliwa kutoka pande zote nne za dunia, kutoka miisho ya nchi hadi miisho ya anga.
sw.R: Kisha atawatuma malaika. Watawakusanya watu ambao Mungu amewachagua kutoka kila upande, kutoka mwisho mmoja wa dunia na anga hadi mwisho mwingine.

decisions.choice: gathering the elect from the four winds: as God promised to gather his scattered people
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 30:4 promises to gather Israel even from the end of heaven, and Zechariah 2:6 speaks of the four winds. Now the Son of Man gathers the chosen.

decisions.choice: the four winds: the four directions, everywhere
decisions.reason: The four winds are north, south, east and west.

decisions.choice: from the end of earth to the end of heaven: from every corner of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase joins two Old Testament ways of saying "everywhere": the ends of the earth and the ends of the sky, where they seem to meet.

decisions.choice: the angels, the elect: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "his angels" and "his elect", as in Matthew 24:31. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: God's chosen people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose chosen people they are, as in 13:20.

decisions.choice: upepo wa pande nne (L); pande zote nne za dunia (B); kila upande (R)
decisions.reason: The four winds mean every direction (meaning decision m2). "Pepo" is the plural of "upepo" but also the word for evil spirits, so Literal keeps the winds with "upepo wa pande nne" and Balanced and Readable say the directions, as in Matthew 24:31.

source.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς ἁπαλὸς γένηται καὶ ἐκφύῃ τὰ φύλλα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: From now the fig tree learn the parable: when already the branch of it tender becomes and puts out the leaves, you know that near the summer is.

en.L: Now from the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already become tender and puts out the leaves, you know that the summer is near.
en.B: Learn this parable from the fig tree. Once its branch turns soft and its leaves sprout, you know summer is close.
en.R: Learn a lesson from the fig tree. When its branches get soft and green and new leaves begin to grow, you know that summer will soon be here.

es.L: Ahora bien, de la higuera {{plural_you:aprendan|aprended}} la parábola: cuando ya su rama se pone tierna y echa las hojas, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que el verano está cerca.
es.B: {{plural_you:Aprendan|Aprended}} esta parábola de la higuera: en cuanto su rama se pone tierna y le brotan las hojas, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que el verano está cerca.
es.R: {{plural_you:Aprendan|Aprended}} una lección de la higuera. Cuando sus ramas se ponen tiernas y verdes, y empiezan a salirle hojas nuevas, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que pronto llegará el verano.

sw.L: Basi kutoka kwa mtini jifunzeni mfano: tawi lake likishakuwa laini na kutoa majani, mnajua kwamba kiangazi [kiko] karibu.
sw.B: Jifunzeni mfano huu kutoka kwa mtini. Tawi lake linapokuwa laini na majani yake kuchipua, mnajua kwamba kiangazi kimekaribia.
sw.R: Jifunzeni somo kutoka kwa mtini. Matawi yake yanapokuwa laini na mabichi, na majani mapya yanapoanza kuchipua, mnajua kwamba kiangazi kinakuja hivi karibuni.

decisions.choice: the fig tree's leaves: a sign of summer
decisions.reason: Most trees in the land of Israel keep their leaves all year. The fig loses its leaves in winter, and new ones come late in spring, so its leaves are a sure sign that summer is near.

decisions.choice: parable: a comparison that teaches a lesson
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a short comparison from nature.

decisions.choice: the fig tree: perhaps recalling the fig tree of 11:12-14 and 11:20-21
decisions.reason: Earlier a fig tree without fruit stood for judgment. Here the fig tree's new leaves show that something is near.

decisions.choice: lesson
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Readable avoids "parable". Here the word means the lesson the fig tree teaches.

decisions.choice: kiangazi (the hot, dry season)
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel summer is the hot, dry season after the rains (meaning decision m1). "Kiangazi" is that season in East Africa, as in Matthew 24:32.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.

records.literal_gloss: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that near it is at doors.

en.L: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that [it] is near, at [the] doors.
en.B: So too with you: when you see these things happening, be sure that it is near, right at the door.
en.R: In the same way, when you see these things happening, you can be sure that the time is near. It is right at the door.

es.L: Así también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} que suceden estas cosas, {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} que está cerca, a [las] puertas.
es.B: Lo mismo {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} que estas cosas suceden, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} por seguro que está cerca, ya a la puerta.
es.R: Del mismo modo, cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} que pasan estas cosas, {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} estar seguros de que el momento está cerca. Ya está a la puerta.

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo nanyi, mtakapoona mambo haya yakitokea, jueni kwamba ni karibu, milangoni.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo nanyi: mtakapoona mambo haya yakitokea, jueni kwamba ni karibu, mlangoni kabisa.
sw.R: Vivyo hivyo, mtakapoona mambo haya yakitokea, mnaweza kuwa na hakika kwamba wakati umekaribia. Uko mlangoni kabisa.

decisions.choice: is near: the subject is not stated; the end, or the coming of the Son of Man
alternatives: he is near: the Son of Man himself
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject, so it can mean "it is near" or "he is near". Luke 21:31 says "the kingdom of God is near". The coming of the Son of Man in 13:26 is what is near in either reading.
